leading_positions.synthesis: Three members prefer optical lattice clocks, all with the same two-name configuration (Hidetoshi Katori, Jun Ye) and a citation built on magic-wavelength trapping and accuracy near 1e-18. They share the view that the physics is mature, independently reproduced, and cleanly attributed. They differ in emphasis: Kroll weighs the capability to measure new physics, Lindroth the control of systematics, and Pearce the convergence of opening support and the instrument-building case. All three record the same open reservation, novelty after the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize, together with the omission of other lattice-clock groups. Pearce moved to this position from IceCube (B043) after the opening ballots, and the chair's own support should be weighed accordingly.

Three members prefer topological insulators with the identical trio Charles L. Kane, Eugene J. Mele and Laurens W. Molenkamp, citing the Z2 classification and quantum spin Hall effect with its HgTe realisation. They share the view that it changed how band insulators are classified and has roughly two decades of independent confirmation. Eriksson moved to this position from DMFT (B046) after the opening ballots. Citation wording differs: Eriksson adds language about topology as a classifying principle of band structure, while Mehlig and Olsson prefer a narrower statement tied to the prediction and the HgTe realisation. All three acknowledge that Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and Hasan lie outside the trio but weigh that cost differently. Danielsson, who prefers B034, would use Hasan in place of Mele in a B016 trio; Eriksson, Mehlig and Olsson explicitly reject that substitution.

Danielsson alone prefers magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (Allan H. MacDonald, Pablo Jarillo-Herrero, Rafi Bistritzer), valuing the pairing of the flat-band prediction with the observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states, and its broad opening support (eight rankings, highest Borda total). Danielsson concedes that the pairing mechanism is unsettled and that first-author experimentalists such as Yuan Cao are outside the credited names. B034 is a stated alternative for Eriksson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce, so it has wide secondary support but a single explicit first preference.

Johansson alone prefers circuit quantum electrodynamics (Alexandre Blais, Andreas Wallraff, Robert J. Schoelkopf), arguing two decades of independent confirmation and its role as the architecture of superconducting processors. Johansson discloses a conflict and acknowledges both the proximity to the 2025 prize on superconducting circuits and the omission of Girvin. Kroll lists B013 as an alternative; Olsson would keep it for a later year.

areas_of_agreement: Every member's preferred configuration is a single-part prize built on one ballot ID, and no member proposes combining ballot IDs in one prize.
B059, B016, B034 and B013 are each described by supporters and critics alike as substantive discoveries; the disagreements concern timing, attribution and category, not whether the science is real.

The Katori-Ye pair for B059 and the Kane-Mele-Molenkamp trio for B016 are accepted by members who prefer other candidates as the natural core of those configurations (Danielsson is the exception on Mele for B016).
Several members state that they would not oppose B059 or B016 as the final prize even where they rank another candidate first (Danielsson, Eriksson, Johansson, Mehlig and Olsson on one or both).
Members who discuss B034 agree that any citation should be limited to the predicted flat bands and the observed correlated and superconducting states, not a settled pairing mechanism.
B046 (DMFT) has explicit round-1 support from no member; Eriksson has moved away from it as a preferred prize, and no colleague defended its attribution.
scientific_disputes: Whether optical lattice clocks are a distinct physical advance (parallel interrogation of many neutral atoms with the light shift engineered away) or a refinement of the frequency-comb and ion-clock lines recognised in 2005 and 2012. Mehlig, Eriksson, Johansson and Olsson raise this; Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce answer it, and Pearce asks what the lattice clock added in kind and not only in degree.

Whether a classification of electronic matter (B016) or a measurement capability (B059) is the greater advance. Mehlig, Eriksson and Olsson stress the conceptual change in B016; Kroll and Lindroth stress demonstrated quantitative results and independent reproduction for B059.

Whether the open question of the mechanism in magic-angle graphene should count against B034, or whether discoveries may be honoured before the mechanism is understood (Danielsson holds the latter; Eriksson, Johansson, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce flag it as a concern).

Whether the 2016 prize on topological phases and transitions overlaps with the Z2 classification and spin Hall effect, or whether these are distinct discoveries (Danielsson and Johansson raise overlap; Olsson and Pearce accept they are distinct).

Whether circuit QED is sufficiently separate from the 2025 prize for macroscopic quantum tunnelling and energy quantisation in superconducting circuits (Johansson argues yes; Lindroth, Mehlig, Kroll and Olsson raise doubts about timing or closeness).
attribution_disputes: B016: Mele versus Hasan for the third place beside Kane and Molenkamp. Danielsson proposed Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan at opening; Eriksson, Mehlig and Olsson keep Mele. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and the 3D work of Fu, Kane, Moore, Balents and Hasan remain outside any three-person set.

B059: Katori and Ye against other lattice-clock groups (SYRTE/Lemonde, PTB, NIST/JILA, Takamoto and others). Kroll and Lindroth would keep two names; Olsson asked whether a third name such as Lemonde is justified, and no member has yet identified a distinct conceptual contribution that would justify one.
B034: Yuan Cao and other first-author experimentalists of the 2018 papers, and earlier moire-band theory, are outside the trio of MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Bistritzer.
B013: Girvin and Huang on the 2004 theory and Majer and Koch on the experimental side are outside Blais, Wallraff and Schoelkopf; Devoret is a link to the 2025 prize.

B043 and B019 were not preferred by any member in round 1, but their allocation among collaboration leaders was raised and not resolved: B043 proposals agree on Halzen, Karle and Spiering (with AMANDA and Baikal predecessors noted), while B019 proposals differ on whether Della Negra or Jenni takes the third place beside Gianotti and Virdee.
maturity_disputes: B034 dates from 2018 and the pairing mechanism remains debated; Eriksson, Johansson, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce regard it as possibly early or as needing a narrow citation, while Danielsson regards the observed phenomena as robust and reproduced.

B059: the redefinition of the second has not happened. Kroll and Lindroth say the case should rest on demonstrated accuracy near 1e-18 and not on that prospective payoff; the committee must decide whether to wait or recognise now.
B013: Johansson argues two decades of confirmation and no maturity problem; others see the issue as timing relative to the 2025 prize rather than maturity.
B043: the diffuse astrophysical neutrino flux is secure, but most of it has no identified source; Danielsson, Johansson, Mehlig and Pearce note that the picture is still being assembled.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson directs the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology at Chalmers (superconducting circuits and circuit QED), has worked in circuit and waveguide QED, and names Chalmers colleagues Delsing and Wilson; Johansson flags possible recusal or at least disclosure on B013 and, to a lesser degree, B025.

Kroll disclosed a doctoral-period research stay in John Hall's laboratory and Hall's association with the frequency-comb work on which Ye's group builds, with no documented collaboration with Katori or Ye. This bears on B059.

Eriksson uses dynamical mean-field theory professionally and would be cautious about advocating B046, and also uses electronic-structure methods relevant to B016 and B034, with no personal tie to any credited person.
Olsson notes a Chalmers connection with Johansson; the electron microscopy candidate Olsson would flag for recusal is not on this shortlist.

Pearce (chair) discloses experimental astroparticle and gamma-ray work close to B043 and a CERN-based PhD close to B019, with no documented tie to IceCube, ATLAS or CMS, and claims no conflict on B059.
Danielsson, Lindroth and Mehlig report no specific conflict with the shortlisted candidates.
questions_for_round2: For B059, what did the lattice clock add in kind, not only in degree, to the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, and can a citation separate the many-neutral-atom magic-wavelength concept clearly enough to avoid a repeat reading?

For B016, must the committee choose between Mele and Hasan to complete the trio with Kane and Molenkamp, and would supporters accept a citation that states explicitly that Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and the 3D discovery lie outside the three-person limit?
Could members who prefer B016 or B059 support the other as a final configuration, and what evidence would decide between a classification of electronic matter and a measurement advance?

For B034, can a citation limited to the predicted flat bands and the observed correlated and superconducting states be worded without committing to a mechanism, and does that wording resolve the maturity objection raised by Eriksson, Johansson, Lindroth, Mehlig and Olsson?
Does the committee judge circuit QED (B013) distinct enough from the 2025 prize, and should Johansson recuse or only disclose on B013 and B025 if either becomes a final configuration?

Can any member argue from the primary literature for a distinct lattice-clock contribution that would justify a third name beyond Katori and Ye, or does the committee accept the two-name configuration?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows two three-member positions, B059 (Kroll, Lindroth, Pearce) and B016 (Eriksson, Mehlig, Olsson), and two single-member positions, B034 (Danielsson) and B013 (Johansson). B034 is a stated alternative for most members, so it is treated as a serious candidate even with one first preference. Each leading position carries a specific unresolved question, novelty after earlier prizes for B059 and allocation of the third name for B016, and round 2 should address those directly.
